components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between oceans, air, and land in a continuous loop

components.text: Water is never created or destroyed on Earth. It is constantly recycled, changing between liquid, vapor, and ice as it travels around the planet. This lesson covers the three main stages of that journey.
1. Evaporation

The Sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Heated water molecules gain energy and escape into the air as invisible water vapor. Plants also release vapor through their leaves, a process called transpiration.

components.title: Key idea
components.text: Evaporation is driven by solar energy. Warmer temperatures mean faster evaporation.
2. Condensation
As water vapor rises, it cools. Cooled vapor changes back into tiny liquid droplets around dust particles, forming clouds. This is why you see your breath on a cold day or droplets on a cold glass.

components.title: Key idea
components.text: Condensation releases heat and is the opposite of evaporation.
3. Precipitation and Collection

When cloud droplets merge and grow heavy, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. The water then runs over the land into rivers and lakes, or soaks into the ground as groundwater, and eventually returns to the ocean to begin again.

components.title: Key idea
components.text: Precipitation type depends on air temperature as the water falls.
Worked Example: Following a Water Molecule

components.title: A Puddle on a Sunny Afternoon
components.situation: After a morning rainstorm, a puddle 2 cm deep sits on a warm sidewalk. By evening the puddle has disappeared. Where did the water go?
questions: Which stage of the water cycle explains the vanishing puddle?
What must happen next for the water to fall as rain again?
components.model_answer: The puddle disappeared through evaporation: the Sun's heat gave the water molecules enough energy to become vapor. The water is now in the atmosphere as invisible vapor. As the vapor rises and cools it will condense into cloud droplets, and when those droplets grow heavy enough they will fall again as precipitation.

steps: Evaporation: the Sun turns liquid water into vapor
Condensation: vapor cools into cloud droplets
Precipitation: water falls as rain or snow
Collection: water gathers in oceans, rivers, and ground
components.label: The cycle at a glance

components.text: Self-Check Quiz

questions.question: What energy source drives evaporation in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy heats surface water so molecules escape as vapor.

questions.question: Which process turns water vapor into liquid droplets that form clouds?
questions.explanation: Cooling vapor condenses into tiny droplets, forming clouds.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
